title: Kalshi court losses pile up as judges refuse to block state gambling laws
raw_text: Kalshi is having a bad week in the federal court system. Two circuit appeals courts rejected the prediction market's latest attempts to block state gambling laws in Connecticut, New York, and Nevada. Kalshi is separately facing a new lawsuit filed by the Arkansas attorney general. In all cases involving Kalshi and state governments around the US, the main issue is whether state gambling laws apply to prediction markets despite Kalshi's claim that its platform offers "swaps" that can only be regulated by the US Commodity Futures Exchange (CFTC). The Trump administration is on Kalshi's side, with Donald Trump Jr. serving as an advisor to Kalshi in exchange for a generous equity deal . "Kalshi insists that its products are not gambling," but "Arkansas law is concerned with substance, not semantics," Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin said yesterday when announcing his lawsuit against Kalshi. Kalshi's prediction market lets customers "wager money on the outcome of just about anything" despite the fact that "gambling on an unregulated platform is squarely prohibited by Arkansas law," he said. raw_text: As Democrats blew away their Republican rivals in an unprecedented midterm sweep Tuesday, the Make America Health Again movement also got bowled over, raising questions about the fate of the motley movement. MAHA—which has centered around anti-vaccine activist and current Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.—saw many of its favored candidates and allies lose, while vocal adversaries of Kennedy won. And the coalition was splintering under stress even before the voting started; in recent months, supporters have accused Kennedy and the Trump administration of inaction and betrayals in their two years in power. Now hobbled in Washington, shedding supporters, and showing little to no influence in voting booths, is MAHA on its deathbed? Or will it be reborn—possibly into a new group? Could it be assimilated into a blue platform—after sloughing off the more repulsive, conspiratorial aspects of Kennedy's ideology? These are the questions circling in the aftermath of Tuesday's bloodbath. Read full article Comments

title: Gamers go to ridiculous lengths to "improve" GTA VI with Nvidia's DLSS 5
raw_text: While the upcoming Grand Theft Auto VI won't be available on PC this month, some gamers are making ridiculous preparations to use their PC graphics cards to apply Nvidia's DLSS 5 technology to the console exclusive. On an explicitly unmoderated GTAVI subreddit, user RevolutionaryBus8208 lays out a proposed setup, which runs a PlayStation 5 through a 4K capture card to a PC. From there, the video signal is run through Veyra , an open source tool that can apply DLSS 5's AI-powered "neural rendering" to video content. The result—which also uses DLSS frame generation to increase the 30 fps source to a 90 fps output—is then piped back to a 4K TV, theoretically adding some of the benefits of a beefy PC graphics card to a console-exclusive game. To demonstrate the potential of this setup, RevolutionaryBus8208 used Veyra to upscale the Grand Theft Auto VI Extended Look trailer posted in August. The resulting DLSS-ified version looks a bit better in places, with sharper background elements, subtler shadows, and more believable light scattering on some surfaces. But it also seems a bit washed out compared to the original video's deeper blacks and arguably suffers from an unnaturally smooth "soap opera effect" in some scenes. Read full article Comments

title: Launch HN: Rivet (YC W23) – Scale and Orchestrate Agents on S3
raw_text: Hey HN, this is Nathan and Nicholas from Rivet ( https://rivet.dev ) – a fast, high-density, and scalable orchestrator for agentic workloads using the actor model. Rather than running a heavyweight sandbox per agent, each agent gets a lightweight actor backed by S3. Actors provide a long-lived process for long agent turns, in-memory state for context, a WebSocket server for multiplayer, durable SQLite storage backed by S3, and hibernation when idle. It's a similar model to Cloudflare Durable Objects, but it’s open source and self-hostable. Here’s a video walkthrough: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Ev6I7DOV9c When we went through YC in 2023, we were building infrastructure for multiplayer games like Diep and Krunker. This involved heavily optimizing high-throughput matchmaking, real-time player messages, and blitz scaling. Through that process, we spent a lot of time on workloads where Postgres couldn't keep up with our throughput. We started out by hacking together Lua scripts on top of Redis, but this became too cumbersome to maintain and upgrade. This led us to extend our game server orchestrator to support what we call Rivet Actors today: many lightweight workers with in-memory state and durable storage. By using actors, we were able to serve tens of millions of monthly active users. As agents grew in popularity, it became clear that running agents in sandboxes is inefficient. title: Motorola's new Signature 27 has it all if you can stomach the $1,600 price tag
raw_text: Motorola is patching a hole in its US lineup with a non-folding flagship phone, but the pricing puts this device dangerously close to the company's expensive tablet-style foldable . The long-rumored Motorola Signature 27 is real, featuring top-of-the-line specs, a super-bright OLED screen, and a ton of cameras. But all this high-end hardware won't come cheap in the age of AI. Motorola's new flagship smartphone will run a whopping $1,600 when it arrives later this month. The Signature 27 is a new take on flagship smartphones from Motorola, leaving behind the middling legacy of the Edge series. However, you'll still immediately clock this as a Motorola device due to its distinctive use of materials and Pantone colors. The phone is metal, ceramic, and glass, but the backs are textured polycarbonate. The device comes in Coal Smoke (black) or Capulet Olive (green) colors. The former has a "tactical weave" finish inspired by automotive design, and the latter is "textile-inspired." This device will include the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, the most powerful mobile chip Qualcomm offers right now. While some smartphones have flirted with 16GB of memory, that's less common these days. The Signature 27 will have 12GB like Samsung's base model flagships. However, there's not going to be an upgrade option for more. You will, however, get a generous 512GB of storage. Read full article Comments

title: Agility Robotics' Nasdaq debut invites scrutiny of humanoid robot market
raw_text: Humanoid robots remain unproven at scale and have not yet achieved widespread commercialization, compared with industrial robots that have decades of proven track records in warehouses and factories. That frank acknowledgment is among the risks outlined in a securities filing by Agility Robotics—the first dedicated developer of humanoid robots to become a publicly traded company in the United States. The robotics company, headquartered in Salem, Oregon, previously became the first to achieve full-time commercial deployment of humanoid robots at a customer warehouse in 2024. Now, Agility’s public listing on the Nasdaq stock exchange as of November 5 has come with financial disclosures detailing how the company plans to build a business around renting out or selling humanoid robots to perform manual labor. “When we are doing robots as a service, it is much lower risk for customers to use it because they are getting a return on investment on day one,” Jonathan Hurst , co-founder and chief robot officer at Agility Robotics, told Ars. "Because they're paying a rate that is comparable to the human labor rate, and that makes the economics pretty straightforward.” Read full article Comments

title: Show HN: A decent text-to-image model trained for ~$20K (Apache 2.0 Weights)
raw_text: My brother and I run a 2-person lab that trains our own generative video models from scratch. The ultimate goal is a set of creative tools that make it easier for anyone to make animation. Video models today are too slow/expensive and lack sufficient controls. Creativity is an iterative process. You make, you tweak, you get better. In our opinion, they're not usable yet for storytelling. When we set out to build Linum v3 (our next video model) earlier this year, the primary goal was to bring the cost envelope of inference down significantly. If our model is fast and cheap, it's the first step (of many) towards useful creative tools. Typically, you see "latent diffusion models". A VAE (Variational Autoencoder) compresses the input data into a smaller "latent space" and the diffusion model learns how to generate within this subspace. Over the past few months, we've been publishing our work on efficient pixel-space diffusion models. These throw away the VAE, having the diffusion model learn a latent-space optimized for its exact task. This serves 3 purposes: 1) Simplify Architecture (no 2-stage model training) 2) Faster Convergence (11x faster convergence vs. our latent diffusion counterpart) 3) Cheaper Inference (4x more aggressive token reduction in attention context-windows, without significant loss in quality) This past month we were pressure testing our latest architecture (Pyramid-JiT) by training a text-to-image model longer than the typical one-off experiment. title: Fujitsu ziet toekomst in dynamische samenwerking tussen mens, ai en robots
raw_text: Event | Fujitsu Tech Open House, Madrid Fujitsu verwacht dat ai en robots steeds meer taken overnemen én samen met mensen bedrijfsprocessen aansturen. Tijdens het onlangs georganiseerde Fujitsu Tech Open House in Madrid presenteerde de Japanse ict-groep zijn visie op deze ‘dynamic transformation’, waarbij technologie niet langer alleen processen automatiseert, maar ook bepaalt hoe bedrijven werken en samenwerken. Onder de noemer dynamic transformation kijkt Fujitsu vooruit naar 2035. Technologie moet tegen die tijd niet alleen kantoorwerk automatiseren, maar ook fysieke werkzaamheden en de samenwerking tussen organisaties ingrijpend veranderen. De nieuwe Technology and Service Vision bouwt voort op Fujitsu’s eerdere toekomstbeelden. Waar in 2023 maatschappelijke en ecologische waardecreatie centraal stond, ligt de nadruk nu op het vermogen om continu te experimenteren, te leren en bedrijfsprocessen bij te sturen. Die flexibiliteit is volgens Fujitsu nodig vanwege de groeiende onzekerheid waarmee organisaties te maken hebben. In een eigen onderzoek onder duizend bestuurders uit Noord-Amerika, Europa en Azië-Pacific kwamen cyberaanvallen naar voren als de belangrijkste bedreiging, gevolgd door geopolitieke spanningen, financiële instabiliteit, natuurrampen en een krimpende beroepsbevolking. title: Wolters Kluwer versnelt ai-innovatie
raw_text: Wolters Kluwer boekt solide resultaten en stevent recht af op het behalen van de jaardoelen voor 2026. Met een organische groei van 6 procent (zonder het effect van overnames) in de eerste negen maanden ligt het databedrijf op koers. de operationele winst steeg 10 procent in constante valuta. Cfo Kevin Entricken laat aan ABM Financial News weten erg blij te zijn met de behaalde resultaten . Vooral cloud-software doet het uitstekend: dat segment levert nu al een kwart van de omzet op en de rek is er nog lang niet uit. Ook over de inzet van ai is de financieel topman enthousiast. Volgens hem versterken ai-technologie, de eigen expertise en de data van Wolters Kluwer elkaar perfect: ‘Het is een goed huwelijk,’ zegt hij Wolters Kluwer blijft zich richten op het versnellen van ai-innovatie. De adoptie van belangrijke ai-gestuurde oplossingen binnen de divisies Gezondheidszorg, Belastingen en Juridische Zaken verloopt voorspoedig. Volgens ceo Stacey Caywood zijn belangrijke partnerschappen gesloten waarmee de eigen content en intelligentie worden geïntegreerd in professionele werkprocessen
